reviews.title: Ok, but could be better
reviews.text:
I’ve been using this for about a year or so - I like how well it’s gotten at predicting my period and ovulation. The interface is simple and easy to use. I also really like the partner feature!! But a few problems I have with it: 
1. There are some things it gives insight on that you can only get if it suggests it to you with a chat. Sleep quality in particular is one. I would LOVE to get that update every day and see how I slept, but it really seems like I can only find out if it decides to suggest a “how did I sleep” chat. And you can’t ask about it with the “start a new chat” either since it only gives you the option to start with specific topics. Why have a chatbot feature if you can’t actually interact with it fully and it’s locked to specific topics?
2. I have endometriosis and I wanted to log it as a condition I have so I could track my symptoms better with that context, and so it would finally stop asking me to take an endometriosis assessment based on my logged symptoms. I had surgery and 100% definitively have it. I was only finally get it to able to log it by taking the assessment multiple times and hoping it would finally ask me “have you been formally diagnosed?”  There should be an option to configure or add conditions. 
3. And finally, for a while I was only medication to suppress my period due to my condition. There is not an option to cycle track for something like that (instead of just period as normal or perimenopause). I would like to be able to log my cycle according to my pill days and when I would’ve likely got my period based on that (along with my symptoms since hormonal medications can impact that). That is not a knock against this app like the others, because it would be an added feature, but I think this would really help a lot of people. 

Unfortunately, I’m just not quite getting enough use out of this app to justify continuing to pay for it. I’m sure it works great for a lot of people, but for my specific case it’s just not quite enough (which is ok, I recognize I am not the majority)

reviews.title: Tracking periods & pregnancies
reviews.text:
I’ve been using the Flo app for close to a decade now, and it has ALWAYS delivered! I love being able to log and track my periods so I know exactly what to expect throughout my cycle.
I also can’t say enough about the trying-to-conceive feature. I’m currently pregnant with my second baby, and Flo has been incredibly helpful throughout the process. Being able to track my ovulation dates made it so much easier when we were trying to conceive, and now I can use the app to follow along with my baby’s development week by week.
After nearly 10 years of using Flo, I genuinely can’t recommend it enough! It has been such a helpful part of my reproductive health journey. ❤️

reviews.title: Shoving Subscription in my face and Flo Partner is male centered
reviews.text: I have been using Flo since 2018. I am deciding to delete the app because every time I open the app, it will not leave me alone about a subscription. A subscription to access information about my own health. As if they weren’t sharing and selling our data without our knowledge for years. I have a boyfriend, I had him download Flo so we can do the Flo Partners. It kept asking him questions about sex. About my sex drive. Giving him advice on sexual positions etc. I am on my period. Hearing this made me very upset and uncomfortable. Why was the app telling him a bunch of sexual things and not actually educating him on periods? Not only that, it gave him inaccurate predictions about my symptoms. The worst part, it focuses on ‘male health’ instead of ‘womens health’ on a literal Period app made for WOMENS health. He got a notification labaled as ‘mens health’. This is absolutely disgusting and I al so disappointed. I expected nothing better from a male led app. I will be deleting and I’m never coming back from this misogynistic app.

reviews.title: Accurate predictions and helpful tracking! Would love some added symptoms/birth control options.
reviews.text: I have been using Flo for over 4 years now, and it’s truly helped me learn more about my cycle and how to monitor it. I’ve struggled with irregular periods for the past 6 years, and Flo has really given me some peace of mind with its cycle updates and predictions. I experience blood clots during my menstrual cycle in addition to the bleeding, so I would appreciate an update that allowed me to track blood clots on top of the type of bleeding so I can start predicting when during my period to expect the clots. I also use Nexplanon, and I haven’t been able to figure out how to add that. I know it’s not something you track every day, but it might be nice to be able to add the implant date?

reviews.text:
I just wanted a simple way to log my cycle and symptoms, so I was using the free version. There are way too many popups trying to sell you the premium version, and they make you jump through hoops to close them. 

Anytime you log a symptom, a chat box immediately pops up offering to tell you more about it—and immediately tries to sell you the premium version. I just deleted the app.

I’m sure the app is helpful if you have premium, or are trying to conceive. It just irritated the hell out of me.
